newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing - optimistic M3 target may be reached in 97.
newsitem.headline: Issing - optimistic M3 target may be reached in 97.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Tuesday he saw a good chance that M3 money supply would continue to slow in 1997.
Issing told journalists, "We had started into the year on a high note but recently it has been not so bad and we expect that stabilisation will continue."
Issing also said, "for the time being we are optimistic" when asked whether or not the Bundesbank will be able to reach its 1997 M3 target.
Issing also said that the Bundesbank realises that monetary capital formation is traditionally weak at times of low interest rates.
"This is a phenomenon we have watched before." Recently monetary capital formation has been weak and this has helped fuel M3 growth.
Issing-optimistic M3 target may be reached in 97=2

M3 is one of the Bundesbank's key monetary policy targets. However, Issing said that it was no longer possible to look only at M3 data and automatically determine from that what monetary policy should be.
For example, Issing said the Bundesbank last year cut interest rates even though M3 growth was still high.
